This paper introduces a new dataset containing 1,000 paired images of fundus photographs and retinal photographs for each of 1,000 patients, featuring diagnoses of glaucoma and/or diabetic retinopathy (DR). This collection is the first of its kind to include these specific image pairs. A deep learning model was developed to classify patients into four categories: neither condition, glaucoma only, DR only, or both conditions. To address the scarcity of examples in the category involving both glaucoma and DR, the authors utilized data augmentation and class weighting techniques. Furthermore, to handle the dataset's inherent class imbalance, the researchers applied both data augmentation and weighting strategies. For feature extraction, the study leveraged pre-trained ResNet models, specifically fine-tuning ResNet152V2 on domain-specific data. Two multimodal fusion strategies were examined: early fusion, which combines raw pixel data, and late fusion, which merges the classification outputs from separate modalities. The analysis indicates that late fusion outperforms early fusion. Additionally, the study evaluated various configurations of data augmentation and weighting to determine their impact on performance. Ultimately, the proposed system achieved a balanced accuracy of 70.2% and a Kappa score of 0.48.

The escalating global spread of the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which causes COVID-19, has overwhelmed healthcare systems worldwide. While lung involvement is a common symptom, identifying these issues early is vital for effective treatment. Although lung abnormalities are frequently detected using X-rays, current diagnostic methods often lack the ability to detect early-stage signs. This study introduces a new approach for automatically identifying potential ICU admission cases by analyzing X-ray images through deep learning. The model's predictions are further validated by integrating ICU admission data, achieved by fine-tuning a pre-trained ResNet50 architecture with an auxiliary neural network. Results indicate that this combined methodology successfully distinguishes between patients likely to require intensive care and those who will not.

We examine light propagation through spherical layered materials, noting that transmission eigenvalues are real and non-negative, with transmission eigenmodes exhibiting angular dependence characterized by spherical harmonics. For angular modes of sufficiently high order, we demonstrate that these transmission eigenvalues converge toward unity, effectively approaching null extinction. Furthermore, within certain stratified configurations, we prove the existence of specific radial profiles in angular modes of sufficiently low order where transmission eigenvalues strictly diverge from the unit value. Crucially, for angular modes of sufficiently high order again, we show boundary localization for transmission eigenfields at interfaces between stratified layers, meaning the field amplitude vanishes within the bulk of the medium.

Discovering novel intent categories from user inputs is a critical task for building scalable dialogue systems. Current methods, however, typically depend on extensive annotated datasets for supervised learning, which are both costly and time-consuming to secure. In addition, these approaches often fail to discover true novel intents because they use intention classifiers pretrained on unrelated data. Addressing these issues, we introduce a fresh paradigm that combines a contrastive learning module with a pretrained language model to identify novel intents without additional annotation. Specifically, we employ contrastive learning to derive intent-specific representations that highlight semantic similarities and differences between utterances. Furthermore, we utilize a layer from a language model pretrained on vast corpora to supply high-quality contextual information, enhancing the representation of dialogues. Experiments conducted across two real-world datasets demonstrate that this approach achieves superior performance compared to existing techniques for detecting completely new intents. The source code will be made available soon.

The classification of simplicial abelian groups essentially mirrors that of connected complexes. For a simplicial group $G$, the classifying space $BG$ is defined as the geometric realization of its classifying square, $BG = \text{Real}(G)$. This paper demonstrates that this space corresponds to a generalized classifying space, $BG = \text{Real}(G)$, of the simplicial frame associated with $G$, thereby establishing that the classifying space of a simplicial group is itself a simplicial frame. Furthermore, it shows that this space is universally bundle; specifically, any functorial assignment of simplicial frames to simplicial frames that respects face and degeneracy maps extends uniquely to such a higher-dimensional structure.

"This paper presents an explicit upper bound for the count of subgroups, denoted $N(G)$, in any finite group $G$. The derived formula follows a specific functional form, $N(G) \leq \max\left\{|G|^{3/2}, |G|^{5\alpha(G)/4}\right\}$, where $\alpha(G)$ denotes the maximum possible order of an elementary abelian subgroup contained within $G$. This result supersedes the earlier bound $N(G) \leq |G|^{3\alpha(G)/4}$ proposed by Huppert and Isaacs, which was based on the maximum order of an abelian subgroup. Furthermore, the authors demonstrate that their new bound is sharp in cases where $G$ is a $p$-group."

This study re-examines the Adler-Bobenko-Suris H_2 discrete nonlinear equation through the lens of discrete linear problems and their associated Darboux transformations. By integrating techniques from multiple scalar linear equations with difference operators, we establish a linked framework involving three discrete spectral problems. The interplay among these systems yields a comprehensive set of distinct, non-trivial Darboux transformations, which form the basis for a refined Bäcklund transformation specific to the H_2 equation. Furthermore, we derive an extended Lax pair structure, illustrating a direct relationship between the original H_2 equation and a new class of coupled nonlinear difference equations.

This paper introduces a new Visual Relationship Detection (VRD) dataset, VisualRelations, designed to address the current lack of data for false positive mining in existing VL datasets. Constructed through a two-stage pipeline—beginning with candidate generation via a pre-trained large vision-language model and followed by human-in-the-loop verification—VisualRelations features 300,000 annotated training samples containing approximately 100,000 false positives. By leveraging this data, we trained a two-tower network that significantly enhances the reliability of relationship prediction in visual-and-linguistic reasoning.

A weak measurement allows for the precise reading of an observable with only minimal disturbance to the quantum state. This study quantifies the weak measurement disturbance by calculating the correlation cost of the pre- and post-selection phases, demonstrating that this correlation cost correlates with the weakness of the measurement. Furthermore, by employing the von Neumann entropy of pre-selection and post-selection states, we present a practical method to assess both the weak measurement disturbance and its correlation cost.

Social relationships are vital for understanding human behavior, yet extracting them from text remains difficult because they are expressed in diverse formats, such as "John is a friend of Jane's," "Jane's friend John," or "John, Jane's, and Bob's friendship." To address this, we introduce an innovative language model that generates social relations as structured, directed graphs consisting of nodes for individuals and edges for their relationships, complete with specific relation types. By integrating a Transformer encoder to process linear inputs with an output module designed to create these graphs, our approach effectively captures both input semantics and the syntactic nuances of social interaction phrases. Evaluated against a dataset of over 100,000 social social media posts, the model demonstrated excellent performance, surpassing existing state-of-the-art text extraction methods.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have established themselves as the standard for most computer vision applications. However, recent research indicates that network depth is the primary factor influencing performance gains, creating significant challenges in efficient architecture design and training. While Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) offer an alternative depth-independent approach, they struggle with efficiency in processing static images. This study introduces a solution by adapting message passing networks, originally designed for graph-structured data, to image recognition tasks. We dynamically construct graphs where nodes represent image patches and edges encode the spatial relationships between them. To maintain translation equivariance, we develop a node ordering strategy that generates prediction-invariant graphs. Experiments on the ImageNet dataset demonstrate that this method matches the performance of CNNs while sustaining comparable training and inference speeds.

Multiple Constant Multiplication (MCM) is vital for numerous digital signal processing (DSP) applications. Existing methods typically prioritize minimizing the count of 1-bit multipliers, often overlooking the specific cost associated with those units. This paper introduces an innovative approach to DSP design by proposing the calculation of fewer 1-bit multipliers with enhanced efficiency per multiplier, specifically addressing hardware cost optimization.

Quantum machine learning (QML) represents a rapidly evolving field within quantum computing designed to solve machine learning problems using quantum algorithms. Initial QML applications indicated that these methods could surpass classical counterparts in both learning capabilities and computational efficiency. However, significant obstacles remain, preventing the widespread adoption of QML in the near future.

To address these barriers, quantum neural networks (QNNs) have emerged as a promising solution. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the QML landscape, detailing its various models, applications, and benefits alongside the inherent challenges. Furthermore, it examines the structure, operational mechanisms, and application areas of quantum-based deep learning, specifically focusing on the role of QNNs. The authors also highlight current research trends and future directions in the sector. Ultimately, this work serves as a detailed resource for researchers and engineers interested in advancing quantum artificial intelligence.

Radio frequency (RF) acceleration technology has been a cornerstone of high-energy physics research for over a century, and this report provides a comprehensive overview of current and ongoing RF accelerator developments in the United States, aligned with the relevant sections of the 2021 Snowmass Vision Document. It examines the status of conventional superconducting technologies, including niobium and alternative materials, as well as novel concepts such as room-temperature acceleration and plasma-based methods. The discussion highlights significant developments in these areas, noting that the provided analysis has been refined based on further contributions received post-submission.

The LHC's observed Higgs boson offers compelling reasons to investigate the electroweak sector with enhanced precision, a goal for which a muon collider represents an unmatched facility. This paper outlines the scientific case for the muon collider, details the project's rationale and vision, and examines the technical hurdles—primarily beam decays and detector design—while highlighting the need for focused, collaborative research and development efforts.

We investigate the dispersion relations of linearized perturbations within a viscous fluid, applying a causal framework to a generalized viscous hydrodynamic approach. This study identifies stability conditions for the dispersion relations of viscous fluids and presents findings from a numerical analysis of different transport coefficients.

We investigate the background radio photon emission resulting from radio recombination lines (RRLs) produced by primordial black holes (PBHs). If PBHs constitute a portion of dark matter, their accretion of interstellar gas in galactic cores would trigger Hawking radiation that ionizes surrounding gas, creating exospheres capable of sustaining PBHs in metastable charged states. Within these exospheres, charged PBHs emit RRLs analogous to those from neutral hydrogen. We calculate the cumulative emission from both charged and neutral PBHs across various RRL transitions. Our findings indicate that the total background intensity from these lines could reach up to $10^{-14}$ to $10^{-13}$ photons per second per cubic centimeter per hertz per steradian, depending on the specific transition involved.

We introduce the Virtual Secure Platform (VSP), a processor architecture designed to execute multi-party computation (MPC) protocols directly on a microprocessor using Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) and the Fully Transferable Fully Homomorphic Encryption (TFHE) scheme. The VSP leverages a dedicated security coprocessor to manage cryptographic operations, freeing up the main processor to handle data processing tasks. We describe the overall architecture and highlight key design innovations, including mechanisms for low-level resource sharing, the adaptation of standard binaries for secure environments, and the integration of an operating system. On the VSP, participating parties can jointly compute over a shared binary without revealing their private inputs to one another. We outline our proposed three-stage pipeline, which consists of an Input Stage, a Compute Stage, and an Output Stage. We have developed a specialized, input-driven scheduler that enhances the main processor's utilization by effectively managing these computation phases. We also present optimizations within each stage to reduce the consumption of computational and memory resources. Empirical results demonstrate that the VSP successfully executes non-trivial workloads, specifically the knapsa cipher and the knn algorithm, using real-world datasets.

The central challenge investigated in this paper involves finding $\alpha$-approximate solutions for constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) featuring arbitrary domains and arbitrary sparsity limits. The core question addressed is whether the sparsity threshold $\delta$ allows for a polynomial algorithm achieving a factor $\alpha = \alpha(\delta)$ that approaches 1 as $\delta$ tends toward infinity. This issue was initially highlighted by Dvořák in 2011 for binary CSPs, who established that a positive answer exists for instances containing at least one solution with density $\delta \geq (1+\epsilon)\log_{1+\epsilon}r$ for any $\epsilon > 0$. Building on this, subsequent research by Dvořák and others (2015) extended the result to sparse instances with domain size $r$ and density $\delta \geq r^{1/\epsilon}$ for every $\epsilon > 0$. The present study generalizes these findings to CSPs with finite valuations, demonstrating that for a fixed complexity class $\Gamma$, there is always a $\delta = \delta(\Gamma, \epsilon)$ sufficient to guarantee an $\alpha$-solution with approximation ratio $\alpha(\delta) \to 1$ as $\delta \to \infty$. The methodology relies on a refined application of the configuration linear programming relaxation, specifically utilizing a novel, more precise upper-bound estimation for the configuration LP's objective function.

Pretrained language models have significantly advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) research, yet their utility in unsupervised or few-shot semantic parsing remains largely untapped. This study investigates whether such pretraining can enhance semantic parsing capabilities. We introduce two approaches: an unsupervised method that fine-tunes a language model on a small annotated dataset while leveraging a knowledge base (KB) for KB-aware token classification to generate semantics for unannotated examples via inference; and a few-shot technique that adapts in-attention mechanisms from the pretrained model to the task by adding minimal task-specific annotations, thereby enabling effective learning from limited data. Evaluations using UNIFIEDPARSE across both data settings demonstrate that these methods substantially outperform strong baselines, with the few-shot approach achieving results comparable to extensive datasets.

High-resolution hyperspectral images (HSIs) offer rich spectral and spatial details, making them ideal for precise semantic segmentation. While strong supervised learning methods leverage HSI features for accurate segmentation, they demand extensive manual pixel-level annotations, which are costly and labor-intensive. To address this, the current study proposes a framework for weakly-supervised semantic segmentation that utilizes hyperspectral data to automatically generate pseudo-labels for high-precision segmentation. By integrating multi-dimensional HSI characteristics, the method designs a weakly-supervised pseudo-label generation module that employs spectral-spatial attention networks to create robust self-supervised labels. Furthermore, the proposed architecture employs a multi-task learning approach with dual segmentation networks to refine these pseudo-labels into final high-quality segmentation maps. Comprehensive experiments conducted on the HyPerSICAD dataset demonstrate that the approach significantly outperforms standard weakly-supervised segmentation techniques.

The massive star HD 108156, a solar-type object with a mass of 0.8 solar masses, is currently in the subgiant phase of evolution. Its spectrum reveals a rich array of molecular bands, including TiO, FeH, and CaH, which indicate the presence of accreted material from a companion planet. This paper reports the detection of rotational broadening in HD 108156's spectral lines, with $V \sin i$ ranging between 10 and 20 km/s. This rotation speed is significantly higher than the typical convective turnover velocity of 1–2 km/s expected for a star of this age. We propose that the star's rotation was accelerated by the ingestion of a companion planet, likely during the red giant branch phase. The observed rotation speed suggests that angular momentum is being transported outward over a timescale of approximately 100 million years, a mechanism that is far more efficient than standard stellar mixing processes.

In the RAM model with addition, memory access to any $w$-bit address takes $O(\log w)$ time, while RAM operations on $w$-bit words execute in $O(1)$ time. This note demonstrates that constant-time execution is possible for every basic arithmetic operation on $w$-bit integers provided the input size $w$ is sufficiently large.

Session-based recommendations aim to predict future items by analyzing user session sequences, a process that typically relies on extensive item-dependent labeled data. To enhance session-based recommendation models, this study introduces a self-supervised graph neural network (GNN) framework utilizing co-training, designed to generate novel session representations and reduce reliance on specific item labels. The method constructs two distinct GNNs, each processing unique self-supervised views of the session data to create complementary predictions. These mechanisms are integrated with session transition probabilities to produce unified recommendations. Empirical results across three public datasets confirm that this approach significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art session recommendation systems.

We define these concepts rigorously, provide several constructions, and establish the necessary and sufficient conditions under which an LCD code qualifies as group LCD or group reversible LCD. Detecting changes in multispectral data is vital for various remote sensing applications, including urban planning, environmental monitoring, and military operations. While many existing change detection techniques are limited to the visual spectrum, our study introduces a new unsupervised method specifically for detecting bi-spectral changes in hyperspectral images. We propose an end-to-end deep learning architecture that utilizes feature fusion within Convolutional Autoencoders to identify alterations between two hyperspectral maps. The process begins by extracting features from all channels in each image plane and merging them to create a composite representation. This integrated feature map is then analyzed by the autoencoder to pinpoint discrepancies. We evaluated the proposed method using the University of Maryland hyperspectral dataset, comparing its performance against established change detection benchmarks. The results indicate a superior score of 0.8255 in the F1 metric, demonstrating significant improvement over comparable existing approaches.

Let $Q_n$ represent the collection of squares of the first $n$ natural numbers. Our study examines the parameter $s(Q_n)$, defined as the smallest integer $t$ for which there exists an additive sequence of length $n$ comprising elements from $Q_n$. Our findings show that for every $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists a specific $n_0$ such that $s(Q_n) < (n)^{0.5 + \varepsilon}$ for all $n \geq n_0$.

This study presents a first-principles investigation into the short-range mechanisms of electron-atom interactions in silicon, with a specific focus on how interference between electron wavefunctions and silicon orbitals influences scattering. We examine elastic and inelastic processes occurring when a δ-function potential is replaced by silicon's ground state orbital, subsequently modeling silicon's more accurate ground-state electron density. Our findings reveal that inelastic events primarily result in excitations from silicon's highest occupied to its lowest unoccupied orbitals. Furthermore, we analyze how these electron-atom interactions impact the broader electron-electron system by modeling a simple square lattice of atomic orbitals. We examine how a single incoming electron induces various collective states, including single-particle excitations, hole-particle pairs, and valley interference states. Notably, we find that inelastically scattered electrons can cause significant long-range shifts in the system's Fermi energy.

Optimization methods are essential for solving real-world challenges, yet developing new algorithms is labor-intensive and requires a deep understanding of mathematical foundations, with no current software supporting every existing method. To address this, we introduce LibOPT, an open-source Python library that integrates various established optimization techniques to enable rapid algorithm development and testing. LibOPT features a modular, object-oriented design that facilitates the easy creation of hybrid methods and allows for simple customization to suit specific needs. Additionally, we have created LibOPT-Networks, a specialized extension for differentiating and applying parameterized optimization algorithms within deep learning contexts.

For a homogeneous algebraic variety $X$ over an arbitrary field, we determine the precise dimension threshold at which the associated algebraic group variety becomes commutative. Additionally, we establish the non-homogeneity of central-isotypish homogeneous varieties whenever their dimension exceeds 2.

This study investigates how particles behave within non-commutative geometries by deriving their dispersion relations through the modified Schrödinger equation. The analysis focuses on the Hessian of the modified energy-momentum function to explore two non-interacting particle systems: first, a spinless pair where the Hessian's determinant signals a modified attractive Coulomb potential that supports bound states; second, a fermionic pair analyzed via both the Pauli and Dirac equations. The Dirac equation approach treats the fermions as interacting with an external electromagnetic field. For both interaction types—Coulomb and external magnetic fields—the modified system yields distinct energy spectra compared to standard models. Specifically, the calculated binding energy shifts for Coulomb interactions and the Landau level structures for magnetic interactions demonstrate clear non-trivial deviations caused by the non-commutative space-time effects.

We introduce a novel charge transport measurement method utilizing nanosecond pulsed, tunable lasers to induce a transient current via two-photon absorption in diamond. This technique enables the mapping of charge carrier dynamics in three dimensions by adjusting the laser excitation focus. Experiments on synthetic single-crystalline diamond revealed charge carrier lifetimes of approximately 100 ns at a charge density of $10^{11} \text{ cm}^{-3}$. Furthermore, the study details the charge carrier mobility and diffusion coefficient as functions of the electric field, noting that at an electric field strength of $10^4 \text{ V cm}^{-1}$, the mobility is $1000 \text{ cm}^2\text{V}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}$ and the diffusion coefficient is $3400 \text{ cm}^2\text{s}^{-1}$.

The rise of harmful content on social media platforms has prompted extensive research into its identification. This study specifically addresses two critical issues: identifying derogatory comments targeting women (often termed misogyny) and categorizing such language into various forms, including insults, threats, and degradation. Our focus centers on the Arabic language, noting a notable scarcity of research dedicated to Arabic misogynistic content. To tackle this, we introduced a multi-task deep learning framework designed to simultaneously identify and classify Arabic misogyny. Additionally, the paper introduces a new dataset derived from Twitter, comprising over 20,000 labeled examples of both offensive comments and specific types of abuse directed at women. Finally, the proposed method is rigorously evaluated to demonstrate its efficacy.

This paper investigates the solvability of fractional backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) with delayed generators in the sense of Caputo. We establish both solvability and uniqueness for this class of BSDEs, where the drift function exhibits Lipschitz continuity across its entire domain and the primary dynamics involve a fractional order $\alpha$ satisfying $2>\alpha>1$. The demonstrated existence and uniqueness rely fundamentally on the equivalent relationship between the CPuto derivative and the Resolvent family of the operator $\mathcal{A}$.

Reinforcement learning (RL) is increasingly employed to solve high-stakes control problems due to its ability to efficiently discover effective strategies for complex, dynamic systems. However, ensuring the robustness and safety of learned policies within RL remains a significant hurdle. This study introduces a hybrid approach that integrates probabilistic modeling with policy optimization to teach controllers capable of executing tasks amidst uncertainty and disturbance. Specifically, the method employs world models to predict system behavior, allowing for reward maximization under scenarios of noise and corruption. By leveraging model uncertainty to guide the policy learning process, the approach enhances the efficiency of RL and yields controllers that are both sample-efficient and robust. Experimental evaluations across physical robotic manipulation and locomotion tasks confirm the method's superior robustness and sample efficiency compared to current state-of-the-art techniques.

This paper investigates the pole cancellation behavior of non-tempered Eisenstein series for $GL(n)$ over rationals, specifically within the context of central critical values of their associated standard $L$-functions.

Addressing the safety challenges inherent to mobile robotic arms, this study introduces a control method based on hierarchical barrier function separation. The proposed system is divided into an upper-level controller that plans configurations to avoid static obstacles and a lower-level controller that ensures safe execution of those plans. To achieve dynamic real-time safety, the barrier differential equations within the lower-level controller are adjusted based on the velocity induced by configuration planning. These adjustments are implemented via control barrier functions (CBFs) within a quadratic programming (QP) framework. Furthermore, the method ensures constraint adherence by incorporating joint limits into the CQp problem. Experimental results on a mobile robot arm demonstrate the approach's capability to navigate dynamic obstacle avoidance tasks safely.

Natural language processing (NLP) has become a vital area of research within the IT sector, largely due to the rapid expansion of unstructured text on the internet. This deluge presents significant challenges, particularly in extracting meaningful information from lengthy documents to create concise summaries. This study proposes a novel extractive summarisation technique that represents text as a graph, where words serve as nodes and syntactic dependencies act as edges. By employing sentence-level features to calculate the betweenness centrality of each word-node, the method identifies sentence importance. Furthermore, specific keywords are extracted from resulting sentences using part-of-speech tagging, with final sentence selection achieved through a threshold applied to a sentence-level feature derived from the text graph.

This demonstrates that coupling a Bose-Einstein condensate with a set of qubits not only enriches the nonlinearity available for quantum logic operations but also provides a flexible framework for generating various nonlinear quantum effects.

This capability is crucial in diverse fields including computer vision, molecular biology, and computer graphics. The line join feature in vector map rendering allows for visually smooth connections between intersecting lines, a capability supported by modern web vector graphics standards like SLK and SVG. Although these formats natively support anti-join (or anti-alizaing) techniques, web browsers often fail to render this effectively, resulting in visible artifacts. To address the lack of native browser support, developers typically implement custom pixel-level anti-aliasing logic in JavaScript, which incurs significant performance costs. This study introduces a novel anti-join and anti-alizaing algorithm based on trilinear interpolation that runs efficiently on the GPU via a fragment shader. The proposed method is lightweight, integrating seamlessly with existing map rendering pipelines without requiring complex modifications.

Multiquadric quasi-interpolation operators are known for exhibiting significant oscillations. This study introduces a new transcendental RBF variant that maintains positive shape parameters, $\gamma \in [0, \infty)$, ensuring preserved shapes while matching the smoothness of the original multiquadric. This novel RBF is also $(n+1)$-times continuously differentiable, $\gamma \in [0, n]$, and demonstrates superior accuracy in numerical tests.

Pulsar halos are proposed as extended gamma-ray emission zones surrounding the pulsar, generated by Poynting-Robertson drag. This phenomenon arises when relativistic pulsar wind particles decelerate due to interaction with the interstellar medium, producing a gamma-ray halo that diminishes with distance from the source. As an observable signature, pulsar halos enable researchers to investigate the dynamics of individual pulsars within the Galaxy. This study calculates the characteristic decay time for pulsar wind particles to form such a halo and evaluates the corresponding spectral luminosity. We further examine the spectral characteristics and spatial extent of these halos, concluding that they are most prominent in the GeV range and extend over hundreds of parsecs.

Adverse weather conditions frequently disrupt transportation networks, causing significant economic losses. To mitigate these disruptions, automated weather classification is essential for intelligent systems like Connected Vehicles and Smart Roads. Although current classifiers for this task are limited to working in specific geographic areas with distinct seasonal patterns, this study introduces a novel, large-scale dataset designed for broader generalizability. The paper also presents the first comprehensive evaluation of deep learning-based weather image classifiers, testing various Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) on the new resource. Additionally, the authors explore data augmentation techniques to enhance model robustness. The results demonstrate that a ResNet-10 variant augmented with specific strategies achieved an accuracy of 96.1%, establishing it as the top-performing architecture for this classification challenge.

This study examines how public information dissemination regarding climate change influences social norms within various economic and institutional settings, ultimately affecting individual behaviors. It begins by reviewing current research on the interplay between social norms and factual scientific knowledge, followed by a detailed analysis of information dissemination mechanisms and shifts in societal attitudes toward climate issues. The work then explores how these informational and normative forces reshape behavioral choices, utilizing a specific extension of the SPREL model to demonstrate the dynamic interactions between evolving social standards and factual understanding. The study concludes by outlining prospective research avenues.

Soft grippers offer significant advantages over rigid counterparts, such as superior versatility in grasping diverse objects, enhanced safety, and greater energy efficiency. However, their complex nonlinear dynamics and material viscoelasticity present substantial modeling and control challenges. This study introduces a data-driven approach utilizing Koopman operator theory to model and control soft multi-fingered grippers. An online modeling framework continuously updates a model of the soft structure by streaming sensor data from the actual gripper in real-time. Furthermore, a simple single-input single-output (SISO) controller is implemented to regulate the contact force at each finger, demonstrating the system's effective grasping capabilities and force control precision.

In recent years, various optimization techniques for training deep neural networks have been investigated. Among them, Natural Gradient Descent (NGD) stands out for its theoretical elegance and accelerated convergence, though its computational cost has limited widespread adoption. This work introduces a generalized framework for understanding NGD by deriving it through two distinct methodologies: information geometry and control theory. Utilizing this broader view, we generate multiple variants of NGD, including extensions to stochastic settings and networks with shared weights. Finally, we evaluate these models through experiments on both standard and nonstandard tasks, such as robotic control and semantic segmentation.

Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains the leading cause of cancer-related deaths globally, largely due to its typically late-stage discovery. Although radiological and genomic analyses offer valuable insights for diagnosis and treatment planning, their ability to forecast patient outcomes is limited. This study introduces a multimodal deep learning framework designed to predict overall survival times for NSCLC patients by integrating CT images, radiological reports, and genetic data. A new method for aligning radiological text with corresponding regions in CT images is also proposed to enhance image-text fusion for survival prediction. Leveraging a newly compiled dataset containing comprehensive demographics, radiological findings, genomic information, and survival records for 311 NSCLC patients, the researchers tested their approach using four distinct fusion strategies. Results indicate that the proposed framework outperforms models utilizing only single data types or dual combinations, achieving a concordance index (C-index) of 0.713.

Representing states is essential in reinforcement learning, a challenge made particularly complex by the presence of natural language in both raw inputs and reward signals. This paper examines various natural language state encoding strategies for NLRL, highlighting the advantages and drawbacks of each. Additionally, it explores future directions in representing natural language states for next steps in NLRL.

We introduce a machine learning methodology to estimate the power spectrum of cosmic density from the redshift-space quasar (QSO) clustering template. The proposed algorithm predicts the power spectrum by learning a mapping from QSO power spectra at multiple lower redshifts. The model is trained using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on synthetic data generated via the large-scale structure (LSS) emulator, which produces halo bias and quasar bias maps. The resulting technique successfully recovers the real-space power spectrum for redshifts up to $z=3.0$ and effectively models QSO bias effects. Furthermore, the machine learning approach yields superior performance compared to standard perturbation theory.

This study investigates certain modules associated with differential operator algebra over Lie algebra $\mathcal{D}(\mathfrak h)$, specifically focusing on Weyl algebra $A_1(x\partial_x)$ and its subalgebra of differential operators with polynomial coefficients, $D(x\partial_x)$, where $\mathfrak h$ denotes the 1-dimensional 1-dimensional Lie algebra. We define $U(\mathfrak h)$-freeness for modules over $D(\mathfrak h)$ and present an explicit construction of such free modules. Furthermore, we demonstrate that every $D(\mathfrak h)$-module of finite length is isomorphic to a quotient of a free module, establishing that the category of such modules possesses properties analogous to those of group rings. Additionally, we analyze specific modules over $D(\mathfr h)$ including those of the form $U(\mathfr h)/J$ where $J$ is a maximal ideal, as well as modules of the form $U(\mathfr h)/I$ where $I$ is a proper ideal. We also examine the structure of the first Ext groups for these quotient modules.

This paper presents an end-to-end Sentiment Analysis framework for retweets on Twitter, leveraging Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. The proposed approach eliminates the need for external dependencies such as part-of-speech taggers, knowledge graphs, or sentiment lexicons. We present two primary contributions: (1) a new data preprocessing technique that encodes retweets using the presence or absence of specific words, and (2) the development of an LSTM model capable of ingesting this specialized input to accurately determine the sentiment of each retweet.

We introduce a dataset and a corresponding dialogue system designed to address the challenge of open-ended, role-specific conversation. Our new corpus, which features 1,000 exchanges (2,000 total utterances) involving a human participant and a computer agent, was created through expert interviews to evaluate candidate models. The data was generated using GPT-3 to explore a diverse range of potential agents, with an average of 11.5 distinct topics identified per expert. To identify the most promising topics for broader application, we employed GPT-4 to analyze these results for diversity and topic coverage. Utilizing this enriched dataset, we developed a scalable dialogue system powered by GPT-3 that adopts a specific persona. The system's capacity for sustained, coherent multi-turn communication aligned with its designated role was verified.

Gravitational wave memory refers to a permanent strain change resulting from the distortion of spacetime caused by distant events. Although individual memory signals are typically buried in noise, a stochastic background may become detectable if such signals are prevalent among compact binary coalescences. We present the first direct calculations of the stochastic background specifically arising from gravitational wave memory. By modeling the source population using recent binary black hole merger rate measurements from the LIGO-Virgo catalog, we estimate the resulting signal amplitude. Our findings indicate that the contribution from linear polarization modes could be as strong as $10^{-9}$ times the amplitude of the dominant circular polarization mode.

Supersymmetry (SUSY) offers a compelling framework for addressing SUSY-breaking mechanisms. We investigate scenarios where this breaking occurs via a first-order phase transition around the $10^{15}$ GeV scale, coinciding with the generation of baryons through leptogenesis. In this model, the decay of generated black holes by the first-order transition can account for the observed abundance of dark matter. Furthermore, the energy scale of gravity waves resulting from this transition could be probed by future detectors like the Einstein Telescope and LISA.

Semantic communication (SC) offers a promising avenue for emerging 5G and beyond-5G networks by prioritizing efficient transmission of essential message meanings rather than complete raw data. This paper introduces a neuro-symbolic causal signaling framework designed to facilitate semantic communications with emergent capabilities for source understanding, causal causal reasoning, and reliable reconstruction. The proposed model employs a signaling system based on signaling theory to identify and convey only critical source features while leveraging neuro-symbolic architecture to infer causal relationships among them for enhanced interpretation and accurate target prediction. Experimental outcomes demonstrate that this framework achieves superior source modeling and target prediction performance with significantly lower bandwidth usage compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques.

Session-based recommendation aims to forecast the next item within a user session by leveraging session history, a task that has recently attracted significant attention due to the compact nature of sessions that capture immediate user intent. Although numerous state-of-the-art models have been proposed, most fail to effectively handle short sessions or lack mechanisms to generalize session context across boundaries. This paper introduces TCRE, a two-candidate ranking embedding model designed to address these limitations. TCE represents session history using only the first two items from a potential ranked list; these Candidate Rank (CR) embeddings capture both individual item quality and their position. Crucially, TCE can process short sessions by aggregating users' long-term preferences into Candidate Rank embeddings, a process enhanced by a session-aware attention mechanism that weighs historical sessions based on current item candidates. Extensive experiments on four public datasets demonstrate that TCE consistently outperforms current state-of-the-art methods.

We investigate the behavior of colloidal dimers, consisting of two connected active Brownian particles, as they navigate through an environment of active colloidal bath particles. This system is driven by internal motility, resulting in a net self-propulsion force. Our findings indicate that internal self-propulsion causes the molecular dimer to act as an active entity with its own propulsion direction. When these molecular components move within a gradient of an active fluid, they experience a net propulsion force analogous to a swimmer in a non-uniform medium. Consequently, the molecule migrates toward regions of heightened bath activity intensity. We demonstrate that this migration speed surpasses that of an equivalent dual-particle system not internally self-propelled, moving within a passive bath. Furthermore, we examine how the particle pair's translational movement and rotational orientation respond to varying self-propulsion levels and interaction rules, ultimately deriving an effective swimming velocity for the molecule that accounts for these factors.

Discrete Fracture Network (DFN) models are essential for simulating subsurface transport and flow, particularly in DFNs that represent subsurface networks. While various numerical techniques exist for solving these models, many are confined to specific, low-dimensional configurations. This paper introduces a strategy for constructing a conforming multi-dimensional mesh around DFNs of any orientation in three dimensions, facilitating the use of MIMETIC Finite Difference (MIMETIC) techniques. This approach enables the simultaneous discretization of the matrix and fracture domains on a shared mesh, where the matrix is divided into volume control volumes and the fractures are discretized using face-based variables. Because the resulting mesh conforms to both rock blocks and fractures, it accurately reflects the complex geometries inherent in DFNs.

This paper addresses the challenges of collision avoidance and formation maintenance for unmanned aerial vehicles (drones). We introduce a formation maintenance strategy grounded in point-set registration using centroid alignment. During formation maintenance, each drone adjusts its position relative to the new calculated coordinates required to regain the formation. While the initial coordinate update for every drone requires communication among the entire group, avoiding collisions during this adjustment process is based on individual drone calculations. Furthermore, each drone simultaneously minimizes distance to its nearest neighbors to enhance formation stability. Two key simulations were conducted: the first tests distance minimization in a standard formation, and the second examines recovery after the lead drone is removed.

This paper introduces a two-tier heterogeneous Vehicular Network (VNet) architecture designed to enhance communication coverage and data rates. The system comprises a macro tier, utilizing Long-Term Evolution (LTE) cellular links, and a micro tier, consisting of Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communications. To enable seamless interconnection between these tiers, both Roadside Units (RSUs) and on-board Vehicle Relays (VRs) are employed. To address the challenge of analyzing the complex, coupled nature of this hybrid system, a Matrix-Analytic Approach (MAA) is employed. This method facilitates the modeling of the system's state transitions and the derivation of a Markov chain to represent the overall structure. Leveraging this formal model, the study calculates key performance indicators, including the end-to-end link reliability and the average number of hops required for transmission.

Although Wikipedia is renowned for its high editorial standards, it struggles to effectively manage and remove low-quality contributions. Although established systems exist to identify and remove such content, they rely heavily on human oversight to define quality standards and create labels for training content moderation models. This paper introduces an automated approach that analyzes the editing patterns of users to assign labels to articles previously unannotated by humans. By utilizing unsupervised learning to detect an individual's contribution quality and automate the labeling process, we aim to reduce the burden on human moderators. We present an algorithm that achieves performance comparable to human-annotated datasets and evaluate our method using a novel, large-scale dataset of user contributions.

Knowledge distillation offers a method for deploying models in resource-constrained environments by transferring a large teacher model's capabilities to a smaller student model. Traditionally, this process relies on explicit knowledge through shared loss functions that compare inputs and outputs between both models, a requirement that excludes zero-shot knowledge distillation when dealing with black-box teachers lacking access to internal parameters or training data. This study introduces a decision-based knowledge distillation framework tailored for black-box decision trees. By analyzing the individual decisions of the teacher tree, the method extracts specific sub-conditions to guide the training of the student tree, thereby enhancing its predictive accuracy. Furthermore, the approach extends to zero-shot scenarios using random forests by employing ensemble distillation. This secondary ensemble is trained to replicate the decision-making patterns of the teacher forest, yielding significant improvements in both precision and recall.

This report details the observation of $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ decays and presents evidence for $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_S$ decays, utilizing LHCb detector data collected in $pp$ collisions at center-of-mass energies of 7 and 8 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 5.0 fb$^{-1}$ for the 7 TeV sample and 3.0 fb$^{-1}$ for the 8 TeV sample. The significance of the observed $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ decay is 6.2 standard deviations, while the evidence for $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_S$ stands at 3.2 standard deviations. The estimated signal yield for $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ is $102 \pm 16$ (stat) $\pm 13$ (sys) events, with the ratio of branching fractions $\mathcal{B}(B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S)/\mathcal{B}(B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_S)$ measured as $1.

This work presents the application of a duality framework for Topological T-Duality (Class. Quant. Grav. 35, 175001 (2018)) to twisted tori. The authors define such spaces as torus quotients by $\mathbb{Z}_n$ where the involution exhibits non-trivial fixed point loci, placing them within the category of Orbi-folds. The study applies this Topological T-Duality scheme to these twisted torus Orbi-manifolds, specifically investigating the consistency of various dualities descriptions regarding the $\Omega$-background and the partition function. A key contribution is the derivation of a corresponding duality transformation for the 2-form B-field on these manifolds, which yields a specific B-field configuration on the dual manifold consistent with existing mathematical theories. The results confirm that topological field theories on these spaces constitute a closed system under the established duality rules for Topological T-Duality.

Imitation learning is a well-established domain within reinforcement learning focused on deriving an efficient policy by analyzing expert behavior. A common strategy involves encoding the observed actions into a compact representation that guides the agent toward similar behaviors, thereby circumventing the exhaustive exploration typical of standard reinforcement learning methods. However, most current approaches rely heavily on precise action alignment, which often results in significant performance degradation for tasks where action granularity varies. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel Co-imititation Learning framework (CIL) that operates without requiring direct observation of expert demonstrations. Instead of focusing on matching specific actions, CIL induces the agent to acquire a task-relevant skill by leveraging the causal relationships inherent in the environment. We validate the efficacy of this method across various robotic manipulation benchmarks, including challenging variations of the Reacher task, a two-arm drum-rolling scenario, and a multi-step desk cleaning task.

This research investigates codes constructed from the Kronecker product of the Nordhaus-Robinson-Sums sequence and Paley matrices, which are proven to be asymptotically automatic. We also present a method for calculating the Hamming distance of these codes and provide empirical evidence suggesting a lower bound of $\delta \geq 1/4$.

We introduce a novel system for tracking hand movements and reconstructing interactions with objects in the wild, utilizing data from hand-held optical sensors. This framework jointly refines hand and object models while estimating their relative motion from sequential 3D point clouds. By starting with object-specific pretrained parameters and employing a coarse-to-fine strategy, the system achieves robust recovery of geometric and semantic structures even with noisy point cloud data. We demonstrate its utility through applications in reconstructing unknown 3D objects, objects with varying appearances, and tracking hand forms and objects under challenging motion conditions.

This study investigates non-abelian tail-triangle C-groups of rank 4 and with an even interlacing value of 2. For each of the 22 identified symmetry groups, we construct a triangle within a simply connected spherical or flat geometry that exhibits eight distinct edge lengths, four pairs of which are congruent. We present generating sets for each group consisting of two reflections across these triangles, thereby establishing the existence of non-abelian triangle C-groups for all 22 occurring group types. Additionally, we demonstrate that each corresponding group possesses a faithful representation as isometries in a piecewise Euclidean, simply connected complex with finite vertex links, thereby establishing a finite-Kobayashi model for each group type.

Calibrating the depth camera is essential for robotics tasks requiring 3D perception, a process typically dependent on known markers or external sensors. This paper introduces a novel, external-marker-free method that jointly optimizes depth-camera calibration and end-effector pose estimation, leveraging only a RGB camera to track a visible marker attached to the robot's gripper. By formulating the problem as an iterative optimization task, our approach first estimates end-effector poses by tracking the physical marker via the RGB sensor, subsequently refining the depth-camera extrinsics and intrinsics, as well as the end-effector frame, using prior extrinsic knowledge. Optimized through gradient descent, the algorithm effectively aligns the depth camera and robot coordinate systems. Experiments conducted on a KUKA LBR iiwa arm demonstrate that the proposed calibration achieves high precision, while the subsequent pose estimation significantly outperforms standard methods based on IMU and inertial measurements.

This paper examines Treatment Interference, or Herd Effects, within a formal k-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) interference framework. We introduce a discernment method capable of identifying Treatment Interference and估 (estimating) its magnitude, alongside a modified regression analysis approach tailored for experimental data under KNN interference. We evaluate the proposed algorithms through simulations and demonstrate their application using results from the 2012 randomized field experiment on mobile text reminders for voter turnout.

We investigate neutrino production resulting from Dark Matter (DM) annihilation within the dense cores of Neutron Stars (NSs), focusing on a model where the DM candidate interacts with nucleons via a pseudoscalar mediator. Our calculations, which employ the relativistic mean-field framework to determine the final state phase space of fermions, reveal significantly boosted neutrino luminosities compared to standard models involving dark fermions. These elevated energy rates could potentially account for the anomalous X-ray brightness observed in the magnetar SGR J1935+2154, assuming a DM density in the NS core that vastly surpasses the halo density.

UNIONS (Utah Northern Observatory/Utah Northern Observatory) is a large-scale survey designed to image the northern celestial hemisphere in the $u, g, r, i,$ and $z$ bands. Utilizing the CFIS camera aboard the 2.3-meter telescope, it employs a dithering strategy that enables the measurement of surface brightness down to approximately 28 mag/arcsec$^2$ in the $g$-band. This photometric precision, combined with a wide field of view, renders the survey highly suitable for cosmological weak-lensing studies. This paper introduces a streamlined pipeline for automating shape measurements, which is essential for such analyses. The workflow leverages the `photutils` package to detect sources and the `astronomy` and `scipy` modules to compute ellipticity. The algorithm operates on co-added images to maximize signal-to-noise, using point-spread function (PSF) deconvolution to correct for convolutional blurring. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through a comparison of the pipeline's output with that of the public LensModeller tool. Furthermore, we apply this pipeline to a lensing test case using UNIONS/CFIS data, covering a 1000 deg$^2$ region of sky. The resulting mean $g$-band surface brightness profile for this area is presented.

We demonstrate that local complete intersection $k$-rational singularities exhibit the $k$-Du Bois property, while for hypersurfaces, we prove it is equivalent to being rational. Additionally, we prove any local complete intersection $k$-rational singularity is necessarily $k$-rational and $k$-Du Bois within a complete resolution context. These results depend on the observation that the structure sheaf $\mathcal{O}_X$ of such a ring $R$ admits a finite presentation as a relative $R$-module over a smooth algebra, a finding which also yields a new proof of Schlessinger's characterization of rational singularities.

The Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) phase, first predicted in superfluid $^4$He and superconducting thin films, has recently been observed in the polarized spin system of the layered van der Waals magnet $\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{Te}_4$. This work reports on the tunability of the BKT regime in $\mathrm{Cr}_2\textbf{I}_4$ via an external magnetic field, utilizing both experimental measurements and Monte Carlo simulations. By applying a field perpendicular to the spin alignment, the system's effective out-of-plane anisotropy is reduced, leading to the BKT state upon crossing a critical threshold of anisotropy. We provide both experimental and theoretical evidence supporting this mechanism, demonstrating that the resulting BKT phase exhibits a tunable critical temperature. These findings offer a new avenue for exploring low-dimensional magnetism in 2D van der Waals materials.

We investigate a dark matter framework where the leading component consists of axion-like particles (ALPs) and the secondary is sterile neutrinos, with the scenario's parameter space being constrained through radiations generated during the ALP's freeze-out. We demonstrate that this model can account for the entirety of cosmic dark matter, with viable regions in the ALP mass and the sterile neutrons mass states existing at fractional ALP masses around $10^{-2}$ to $10^{-3}$ eV for sterile neutrons with masses spanning from keVs to Mevs. We further explore the cosmological origins of the ALP, specifically examining how string axions and QCD axions can be accommodated within this framework. Additionally, we explore the potential for detecting ALPs via their conversion into photons within a magnetized cavity, noting that the ALP mass must exceed a threshold of approximately $0.17 \mu$eV to be detectable.

Recent years have seen significant theoretical progress connecting magic states to matrix product states, with a key metric being the "stabilizer rank." Lower values indicate greater computational efficiency in simulations. In this work, we establish tighter upper bounds for specific crucial magic states. By applying novel Clifford group properties, we demonstrate that for all single-qubit $T$ gates, the stabilizer rank does not exceed 5. This improves upon the previous best bound of 6 and offers a more than twentyfold reduction from the earlier theoretical limit of 128. Furthermore, we show that magic states representing square roots of Pauli operators possess a stabilizer rank of no more than 2, and those representing square roots of generalized $Z$ require a rank of at most 3. These findings directly expedite near-term, tractable simulation efforts for near-future quantum algorithms.

This study examines a single-component holographic dark energy (HDE) model with a temperature-dependent cutoff, modified by Tsallis non-extensive statistics. The dynamics of this Tsallis HDE are analyzed within the framework of complex quintessence, which is implemented in a Friedmann-Lemaitre-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) universe. The research investigates the behavior of both the real and imaginary components of the complex scalar field, alongside their associated kinetic energy, energy density, equation-of-state (EoS) parameter, and cold roll rate. The evolution of these quantities is visualized across redshifts from $z = 100$ to $0$. The paper further derives the conditions required for both a future cosmological epoch of accelerated expansion and a phase transition between eras, demonstrating that the complex nature of the scalar field is essential for this cross-over to occur.

The LAMOST Time-Domain Survey (LAMOST-TDS) is a project designed to monitor the optical sky ($\lambda$ 3600–4900 \AA) using the LAMOST spectrograph in dual-band filter modes. This monitoring covers 40\% of the celestial sphere with a cadence of approximately 10 days. The K1 and K2 observing modes utilize LAMOST's 4 fiber-fed spectral slitless cameras, observing two adjacent $2^\circ\times2^\circ$ fields simultaneously. This paper details the initial data processing for the first four $K2$ plates, detailing the procedures for flat-fielding, wavelength calibration, and relative flux calibration. True Random Number Generators (TRNGs) are essential for numerous security-critical applications, including cryptographic key generation and random nonce creation. Although TRNGs are typically implemented in SRAMs, these numbers remain vulnerable to attacks targeting SRAM manufacturing variations and aging effects, which can compromise their true randomness. To address this vulnerability, we introduce TuRaN, an SRAM-based TRNG that utilizes voltage underscaling to generate secure random numbers. By applying voltage underscaling to SRAM write operations, the resulting unpredictable power consumption fluctuations are harvested to seed a post-processor and a Cryptographically Secure Pseudo-Random Number Generator (CSPRNG). We evaluated TuRaN's implementation on commercial 65nm SRAM, confirming its ability to produce high-quality randomness and achieving a post-processing-free True Randomness Ratio (TRR) of 99.99999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999

This study introduces a design framework for nonvolatile resistive switching devices based on a single molecule, utilizing a gold breakjunction as the substrate and a central C60 molecule functionalized with a thiol group for the switching layer. The device operates as a single-electron tunneling resistor switch, where resistance variations are governed by electrostatic interactions between the molecule and electrodes, as well as charge within the molecular structure itself. The proposed setup demonstrates superior characteristics, including strong nonvolatility, high resistance ratios, and stable switching behavior. Furthermore, the device exhibits significant resistance modulation in response to gate voltage changes, indicating viable potential for application in future single-electron component systems.

We establish a robust framework for the causal representation of loop Feynman diagrams featuring multiple intersections, even with multiple loops involved. This methodology enables an efficient and precise computation of these multi-loop integral functions, maintaining high accuracy down to the maximum possible order in Taylor expansions around logarithmic singularities. Furthermore, we present streamlined representations for specific singularities and apply this framework to evaluate internal components of the two-loop light-by-exchange diagram, which appears in calculations of the muon's anomalous magnetic moment ($g-2$).

This paper establishes an eigenfunction expansion formula for 1D 2-state quantum walks, serving as a non-unitary analog to Fourier series and the Fourier non-diagonalization of 1D Schrödinger operators. For the matrix-valued Hill equation, we demonstrate the existence and uniqueness of a unique solution that is both bounded and continuous, provided it features a non-trivial trace determinant. Furthermore, under the assumption of periodicity, we prove a corresponding three-wave theorem.

We investigate hybrid stars by integrating the MIT bag model with the MIT or Nambu–Jona-Lasinio (MIT/NJL) model within the framework of the sigma-omega rho (SkR) nuclear interaction model. In this framework, hadronic phases are defined by the SkR potential, while the MIT/NJL descriptions of a quark-gas phase include two-flavor and three-flavor variants. To determine the equilibrium between hadronic and quark phases, we employ the Gibbs criteria. Our results indicate that the inclusion of strange quarks in the MIT/NJL model significantly alters the quark-gas equation of state, causing hybrid stars to exhibit larger radii and higher maximum masses compared to those predicted by the MIT charmless variant. Furthermore, we demonstrate that hybrid stars can exhibit properties consistent with the neutron star PSR J0048-8453, thereby providing evidence for the existence of a quark core within this object.

Controlling electronic and magnetic properties in transition metal oxides via tailored growth conditions offers a promising avenue for influencing fundamental material characteristics. Within this context, density functional theory (DFT) emerges as a powerful tool for characterizing the effects of interfacial strain and electronic charge transfer on magnetic order and electronic structures. This study examines various configurations of d-block metal monolayers and bilayers situated on SrTiO₃ substrates. We evaluate magnetic moments and state densities for these systems, revealing that both strain and charge transfer can induce significant alterations in magnetic ordering and density of states. Additionally, we assess the origins of fluctuations in orbital and spin moments across different monolayer and bilayer arrangements, noting that these internal variations are sensitive to specific atomic positions and symmetry breaking. Ultimately, our findings demonstrate that fabricating multilayer stacks of d-block metals within heterostructures provides an effective strategy for engineering orbital and spin degree of freedoms.

We introduce a quantum stochastic framework to investigate the probability distribution of trapped and cooled laser-atom samples. Our analysis reveals that under typical conditions, these distributions conform to Gaussian statistics characterized by standard thermodynamic temperature and density. However, in specific regimes, the distributions shift to an exponential (Bose-Einstein) form. This anomalous behavior persists even as the atomic number density decreases by several orders of magnitude compared to the quantum degenerate threshold. We attribute this phenomenon to the combined influence of optical lattice dissipation and coherent light-matter coupling, offering a robust mechanism for atomic control through engineered environmental interactions.

This study investigates the inter-trading dynamics within the cryptocurrency trading network, focusing on the time-varying association measures between asset pairs. The analysis reveals that the network's structure remains largely consistent across different timeframes, with the duration of these topological configurations lasting from tens to hundreds of minutes. Additionally, the research examines the dependency relationships among multiple cryptocurrencies simultaneously, modeling the trading dynamics of high-dimensional data using a high-order pairwise copula GARCH model. The findings indicate that the effective dimensionality of the system is significantly lower than the total count of cryptocurrencies analyzed, suggesting a substantial number of underlying latent factors drive the observed behaviors.

Forming new particles from gas-phase components is a critical process within the lower atmosphere. While acid-water clusters are considered essential intermediates in this mechanism, existing models often rely on quasi-chemical assumptions that fail to account for finite cluster size effects. This study employs path-integral molecular dynamics (PIMD) simulations to examine acid-water clusters, specifically $[(\text{H}_2\text{O})_n\cdot\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4]$ for $n=1$ to $4$, incorporating quantum nuclear effects via the path integral method. Our findings reveal that quantum effects, particularly zero-point motion, significantly alter the structural and dynamical characteristics of these clusters. Specifically, we observed a pronounced reduction in both the average residence time of water molecules and the average coordination number due to zero-point effects. These observations suggest that quantum acid-water interactions could facilitate the initial steps of new particle formation more effectively than purely classical simulations predict.

This paper introduces the compactification of perception pairs $(X, \phi)$, where $X$ is a compact Hausdorff space and $\phi$ is a continuous self-map, denoted as $(X, \phi)^+$, alongside the compactification of the relevant function spaces. The motivating application involves the study of spaces containing all group-equivariant non-expansive operators acting on bounded subsets within Hilbertian G-C*-algebras, specifically concerning fixed-point properties related to perceptions. The authors demonstrate that the newly formed space $(X, \phi)^+$ retains the continuity of the map $\phi$ as a self-mapping onto $X$. Furthermore, they establish an isometric isomorphism between the bounded group-equivariant non-expansive linear operators on a Hilbert $C^*$-module $B$ (under a compact group action) and those acting on the space $B^+$, which consists of bounded functions defined on the compactification $(X, \phi)^+$.

A recent theoretical prediction suggests that a Hall response in heat flux can emerge in rigid solids subjected to movement within gravitational fields or acceleration. In this work, we demonstrate that the Hall response manifests even in flexible (non-rigid) non-relativistic, non-equilibrium systems lacking spatial variation, where it arises from the orbital angular momentum associated with vibrational excitations. We further show that this thermal Hall effect disrupts the analogies between thermal and gravitational phenomena and demonstrates that generalized Einstein relations remain invalid in this context.

Recent research indicates that the generalization capabilities of deep learning models are closely tied to their geometric complexity, specifically the sum of the squared norms of layer weights. This paper explores how neural networks minimize geometric complexity alongside other standard metrics like generalization error, training loss, and parameter magnitude. We investigate these phenomena using a linear neural network tasked with learning a mixture of two quadratic functions, where our line network possesses infinite width and applies a specific readout mechanism. Results demonstrate that a linear probe accurately predicts learning progress, including the timing and order in which various functions are mastered. Furthermore, we identify multiple regularizers governing complex learning tasks and offer explanations for the empirical success of L2 regularization in simple over-parameterized settings, as well as the widespread utility of weight decay.

We outline a method for directly extracting the Wilson coefficients of the effective four-fermion operators governing $B^0\to K^{*0}\mu^+\mu^-$ decays. This approach circumvents the conventional reliance on hadronic parameters by leveraging the angular distribution of the $K^{*0}$ system. We demonstrate that the necessary hadronic inputs can be obtained from the normalization of the branching fraction and the $q^2$-dependent coefficients for the longitudinal and transverse polarization of the $K^{*0}$ vector meson. Furthermore, we evaluate the uncertainty associated with the direct extraction of Wilson coefficients and analyze the impact of theoretical and experimental errors on this determination.

Automated essay scoring (AES) represents a critical application in machine learning, a field in which this study investigates the efficacy of data augmentation for enhancing the performance of transformer-based AES models. The researchers evaluated augmentation strategies including back-translation, synonym substitution, and domain-specific techniques. Experiments were conducted on English and Turkish datasets, where domain-based augmentation involved fine-tuning pre-trained models on a small subset of target domain data after initial pre-training on the source domain. Results indicate that the German Espresso model, adapted for English via fine-tuning, significantly outperforms standard in-language fine-tuning approaches. Furthermore, our augmentation-driven English Espresso achieved superior results compared to the baseline English Esporto model. The authors conclude that data augmentation is a highly effective method for boosting AES system performance, particularly in low-resource settings.

We define marginal independence models as collections of probability distributions where specific subsets of variables adhere to particular structural constraints. Drawing inspiration from algebraic geometry, we analyze the shape and defining properties of these model spaces using tools like Gr\"obner bases. Additionally, we achieve a normal form for each distribution within these models by applying the technique of distribution matching. Finally, we establish methods to verify whether a categorical distribution belongs to one of these models by checking for marginal independence across multiple partitions of variables.

This study introduces a dynamic framework for vertical mobility featuring a specific allocation problem. Consider a society divided into two classes based on whether individuals hold a university degree. Government policies, such as scholarships, can be distributed exclusively to university-educated members of the lower social stratum. The central inquiry is how to optimally allocate these programs across a multi-generational timeline to maximize the total number of programs that improve social mobility. The findings indicate that a program's success rate in advancing generations influences future distribution strategies: if a policy proves more effective in a specific lineage, it is likely to receive increased funding targeting that lineage in subsequent periods.

This study derives the link between the phase factor $(-1)^{2s}$ (relating the propagation properties of free particles of spin $s$ to their statistical behavior) by incorporating parity transformations into standard Lorentz boost and rotation symmetries. The non-relativistic analysis relies on three key elements: the transformation rules under Galilean boosts, a generalized time-reversal symmetry applicable to particles with arbitrary spin, and the ability to compose a Galilean transformation with a rotation to simulate a parity flip. The derivation proceeds by demonstrating that the propagation characteristics of moving particles imply invariance along light rays, thereby establishing a relativistic framework even within non-relativistic quantum mechanics.

We introduce a modified RingCT variant incorporating stealth addresses, where the utilization of Zkpads is entrusted to the transaction signer. Although this ring based cryptocurrency maintains full anonymity, it streamlines the signing process by reducing the burden on users. Our implementation demonstrates that this version produces smaller transactions and enhances the user-friendliness without compromising security.

We demonstrate that if probabilistic or deterministic nearly logspace algorithms exist for solving specific structured linear systems, then permanent-based circuit lower bounds apply. Our approach extends a strategy initiated by Kowalski and Vollmer, originally designed for symmetric matrices, to encompass broader non-spectral structured matrices. Consequently, our findings reveal that identifying useful low-depth circuits for these structured matrices could yield meaningful insights into lower bound proofs.
