Gerrymandering, the manipulation of electoral district boundaries to favor a political party, remains a critical issue in the United States despite recent Supreme Court rulings mandating more transparent redistricting processes. While increased transparency has shifted map-drawing tactics from overt cheating to subtler forms, the evolving nature of these methods complicates detection. This study introduces a quantitative metric for evaluating Gerrymandering using redistricting maps from Pennsylvania, a state heavily impacted by the controversy. We also employ a redistricting algorithm based on simulated annealing to generate comparable maps, allowing for the calculation of our proposed metric between actual and synthetic scenarios to assess Gerrymandering levels.

In the domain of patterned fabric defect detection, the calculation of the structural similarity index (SSIM) has traditionally served as the primary method for identifying variations between standard and image defect blocks. However, because SSIM relies on features like luminance, contrast, and structural similarity, it often struggles with real-world textured fabrics, resulting in an inability to precisely distinguish faulty areas. To address this limitation, we introduce a refined approach that integrates Gradient Histograms of Oriented (GHOG) features with low-rank matrix decomposition. By utilizing directionally sensitive GHOG features to enhance feature representation and applying low-rank decomposition to highlight subtle discrepancies more effectively than previous methods, our algorithm successfully identifies defects even in complex patterns. Comparative experiments conducted on two standard datasets demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing techniques, achieving superior accuracy in detecting fabric defects.

This research proposes a novel approach to visual navigation under uncertainty, leveraging information theory within reinforcement learning. Our method utilizes mutual information as a regularization term within the reward function to enhance robustness against navigation targets obscured by occlusion or noise. By integrating this mutual information-based penalty into the learning process, the system ensures more consistent navigation. Experimental results across both simulated and actual driving datasets demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing approaches in terms of navigation efficiency.

Building on the work of Price, we derive a bondy mass loss limit for gravitational waves within the context of linearized gravity on an asymptotically anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetime. By applying a novel technique to analyze the Bondi mass-loss formula, we demonstrate its direct correlation with the standard energy flux formula. This connection allows us to establish a strict upper bound on the rate of Bondi mass evolution. Furthermore, utilizing Price's scattering theory for linearized gravitational perturbations within spherical AdS backgrounds, we verify this proposed bound.

We investigate the gravitational wave signatures produced by compact object remnants from the first generation of stars within nuclear star clusters (NSCs) of early galaxies. Our analysis focuses on two formation scenarios: the collapse of single stars and the collapse of binaries, specifically examining the effects of binary interactions on the resulting compact object mass distribution. We employ the initial mass function proposed by Kroupa et al. (2009) and model the subsequent evolution of these stars using a Monte Carlo technique. By integrating these methods, we estimate the stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB) arising from the stochastic merger of these early-formed black holes and neutron stars. Our findings indicate that the resulting mass distribution for remnant compact objects is highly sensitive to the frequency of binary interactions among stars. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the characteristic frequency of the SGWB generated by these ancient stellar remnants falls within the detection range of future space-based gravitational wave observatories.

The escalating demand for energy has driven a surge in power consumption, a trend that has been met by a strategic shift from fossil fuels to renewable sources like solar and wind. However, the unpredictable nature of these energy sources makes the integration process complex. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a data-centric approach for identifying incidents within the grid, specifically targeting the optimization of energy production and consumption. By leveraging machine learning, the system analyzes historical data to detect anomalies, with a specific focus on outage detection in the context of wind energy. The methodology is demonstrated using real-world data from the Australian Energy Market Operator (AEMO), which details energy flows between Australian wind farms and the national grid.

This study investigates the processes $X(3872)\rightarrow J/\psi \pi \gamma$ and $X(3872)\rightarrow J/\psi \pi\pi \gamma$ within the framework of hadronic molecular models. By employing the quasipotential method, we calculate the relevant wave functions for the $J/\psi(J^{\prime})$ and light pseudoscalar mesons ($\rho$, $\omega$, $\pi$, $K$) to derive the wave function overlaps. Consequently, the branching ratios for these decays are computed, yielding $\mathcal{B}(\Gamma \rightarrow J/\psi \pi \gamma) = (1.0^{+1.1}_{-0.5}) \times 10^{-5}$ and $\mathcal{B}(\Gamma \rightarrow J/\psi \pi\pi \gamma) = (1.1^{+1.1}_{-0.5}) \times 10^{-5}$.

We present a characterization of smooth quadrics by the action of their automorphism groups on the category of coherent sheaves, in a manner analogous to how Langsness previously characterized cubic threefolds. Furthermore, in the course of this investigation, we characterize the ambient linear space $\mathbb{P}^n$ through $\mathrm{Per}(\mathbb{P}^n)$, the permutation group action on $\mathbb{P}^n$, via $\mathbf{P}^n$.

Text-based games offer an excellent framework for assessing language comprehension, complex problem-solving, and planning within both virtual and actual environments. However, existing systems for running these games often suffer from sluggish performance, restricting extensive exploration. We introduce TextWorldExpress, a high-performance engine capable of executing popular instances of these games on a single CPU core at an average rate of 380,000 steps per second. This dramatic speedup enables exploring millions of game states in mere seconds, significantly accelerating the testing of problem solvers. Moreover, TextWorldExpress supports dynamic, programmatic level generation, making it ideal for large-scale simulations to test various solution methods. The engine is built upon a refined version of the TextWorld framework, which provides access to diverse problem-solving strategies and educational opportunities.

The primary objective is to demonstrate the efficacy of this approach in characterizing TI systems containing defects. The analysis begins with a two-electron-irrep (2-D) TI exhibiting straight boundaries, followed by the examination of a TI with the Moiré structure found in twisted double graphene sheets. Subsequently, the research investigates a 2-D TI perturbed by point impurities. The points of interest within the TI are mapped using the Pauli matrix, where the x and y axes correspond to the $\sigma_x$ and $\sigma_y$ components, respectively. We establish precise pointwise and $W^{1,q}$ norm bounds for $p$-harmonic functions defined within planar sectors. For non-zero parameters $p \in (1, \infty)$, these functions admit representation as a sum comprising a linear combination of power functions—specifically $r^{\lambda} f(\theta)$, where $r$ and $\lambda$ denote the radial coordinate and a specific exponent respectively, and $f$ is a particular function of angle $\theta$—multiplied appropriately, alongside a remainder term. Our pointwise convergence analysis reveals that the gradient of such functions decays with a specific order of magnitude determined by the minimum of two exponents, $\lambda$ and $\mu$, relative to the distance from the origin.

This paper introduces a new multivariate spatial model for conditional extreme spatial dependence across the ocean surface. The proposed framework is grounded in the Extremal Spatial Copula for Conditionals (ESCS), initially developed by the authors in an earlier paper. The model is specifically designed to handle scenarios with a high number of dimensions, which are typical in marine science. The study demonstrates its application through an analysis of extreme ocean environments, utilizing a dataset of sixteen environmental variables. The data, sourced from the European Wave and Offshore Validation Project (WAVEWATCH III model), covers the North Atlantic region between 40°N and 60°N latitude from 2002 to 2008. The results indicate that the model effectively captures the conditional extreme behavior of ocean environments.

Driven by the intermediate Lang conjectures regarding hyperbolicity and rational points, we establish new finiteness theorems for non-constant maps from and to fixed varieties defined over a number field, utilizing moduli spaces of maps alongside Faltings's finiteness theorems.

Manipulation capabilities are highly dependent on how well a robot's hand can reach various parts of an object, a property known as manipulability. However, a robot's ability to grasp effectively varies based on how it is mounted; specifically, different attachment orientations result in distinct manipulability maps. This paper introduces a data-driven approach that translates pre-existing robot-manulated object knowledge into new mounting configurations. First, we develop a novel domain adaptation strategy using Parallel Transport to shift manipulability estimates between free-space poses. Second, we introduce a manifold-aware Iterative Closest Point (ICIC) algorithm that aligns feature point clouds while accounting for the specific geometry of manipulability surfaces. Experimental results indicate that this method successfully adapts manipulability domains and substantially enhances overall prediction accuracy.

This study employs the matrix element method to investigate the Higgs boson pair production channel $\text{HH} \to \text{b}\bar{\text{b}}\text{W}\text{W}^{*}$ at the LHC, specifically analyzing the kinematic distributions of the final state objects. The research focuses on the on-shell $\text{W}\text{W}^{*}$ decay mode, where the system decays into electrons or muons accompanied by neutrinos, and the two b-quarks are reconstructed as a single jet. The analysis utilizes a tag-and-probe strategy to identify the lepton pairs, while the missing transverse momentum arising from undetected neutrinos is estimated by matching them with leptons from off-shell $\text{Z}$ decays. The study further details the methodology for estimating systematic uncertainties and demonstrates that the matrix element method effectively enhances the signal-to-background ratio.

We introduce a novel method for learning 3D object pose estimation by leveraging "accidental" instances of rotation found in image sets. While most research focuses on single or dual-view estimation from arbitrary angles, we target scenarios involving multiple images where the objects have been rotated along a single axis of 3D. By utilizing a neural network trained on such data, we successfully estimate precise 3D pose, including yaw (rotation) and roll (inclination), even when presented with images from various viewpoints. We validate our approach using a new dataset of real-world objects that are rotated in place across multiple images, as well as on the standard ModelNet dataset.

This study introduces a novel framework for identifying whether individuals adopt or discard misinformation, specifically concerning the acceptance or refusal of COVID-19 vaccines on Twitter. We introduced the concept of an "adoption network," constructing a subgraph that captures the contextual discourse surrounding vaccine-related tweets. Within this network, we identified linguistic cues signaling acceptance or dismissal of false claims and trained classifiers to automatically detect such signals. Furthermore, we engineered features representing long-range dependencies to model temporal sequences of tweets. Empirical results indicate that our approach successfully distinguishes the adoption from the rejection of deceptive content, offering robust implications for understanding how falsehoods spread and are processed socially.

We introduce a high-yield method for producing intense isolated attosecond pulses by applying strong-field coherent manipulation to the ionization step within High-Harmonic Generation (HHG). By precisely tuning the carrier-envelope phase (CEP) of an infrared driving laser, we observe a coherent enhancement of coherent resonance ionization (CRI) yields. This control over ionization efficiency subsequently governs the intensity of mid-infrared-driven HHG output, resulting in the generation of extremely bright, single-attosecond pulses.

This study investigates the photometric and spectroscopic characteristics of the detached eclipsing binary Algol (Beta Persei) using data from the ASAS-2, ASAS-3, ASAS, and ASASNet projects, alongside 270/458 nm spectral observations. The system's light curves were analyzed using the non-linear least squares method, while the orbital parameters were determined through spectroscopic analysis. Our findings indicate that Algor functions as an eccentric, detached eclipsing binary with an orbital period of 2.867 days and eccentricity of 0.101. The primary star is a B7V-type giant with a mass of 2.500 solar masses and radius of 2.400 solar radii, orbiting a secondary star with an estimated mass of 0.800 solar masses. Additionally, the study estimates the system's inclination angle at 90.000 degrees and the binary separation at 3.800 AU.

We investigate the mass blow-up behavior of ground states for the mass-critical nonlinear equation involving an obstacle. By leveraging a mass optimization constant rooted in variational methodology and applying techniques from the concentration-compactness framework, we derive an upper bound for the associated L²-norm. Furthermore, our results confirm the validity of a sharp mass constraint on this blow-up solution's mass.

Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have proven effective across diverse fields by integrating physical laws into neural architectures for solving inverse and data-sparse problems. However, their practical application is often hindered by slow convergence and poor accuracy. This study introduces Residual-based Adaptive Node Generation (RANG), a novel strategy designed to enhance PINNs. By identifying under-resolved regions through high residual values, RANG dynamically adds trainable node pairs to accelerate learning and refine solution precision. Validation against one- and two-dimensional test cases demonstrates that the method significantly outperforms standard alternatives in both computational efficiency and accuracy.

Multi-terminal multi-domain ferroelectric devices are essential for the accurate study of ferroelectricity and modeling the operation of ferroelectric FETs (FeFETs). This study employs a fully coupled first-principles-based phase-field modeling framework to investigate the nonlinear behavior of electric displacement and strain, as well as the kinetics of domain wall movement within a 2D n-type doped AlScO3 thin film supported by Pt electrodes. The simulation examines the influence of lateral n-type doping on the electric field distribution and domain structures, specifically analyzing scenarios with both uniform and linear doping gradients. Results reveal that domain orientations are dictated by the global energy minimization of the system, while the reorientation of domains due to gate voltage changes is driven by local electrostatic conditions at the interfaces. Furthermore, the study identifies multi-domain configurations capable of producing a negative capacitance signature in the electric field versus strain hysteresis loop, a phenomenon attributed to the complex interactions between domain walls and the electric field. These multi-domain structures also demonstrate the ability to suppress remnant polarization. Finally, the research explores how lateral conductivity variations in the channel influence the domain architecture and the characteristics of the capacitance hysteresis loop.

Software vulnerability research has extensively covered the operating system, network stack, and web browsers, yet these areas often share a common dependency: the cargo ecosystem. This cargo environment serves as a vital source of libraries for numerous prominent projects, including those within the web domain. Despite its significance, the cargo ecosystem has received surprisingly little attention regarding vulnerability analysis. This paper introduces an innovative methodology for examining vulnerability propagation within cargo. First, a knowledge graph dedicated to cargo ecosystem dependency-vulnerability was built to capture the intricate relationship between vulnerabilities and package dependencies. Subsequently, propagation patterns were analyzed by querying this graph using a subgraph mining technique. The findings reveal that vulnerability spread within the cargo ecosystem is highly non-uniform, frequently traversing multiple packages before halting. Furthermore, the research identifies specific "vulnerability traps"—packages characterized by dense internal dependencies that accelerate and intensify the vulnerability attack surface.

This study investigates the ergodic characteristics of the stochastic Ginzburg-Landau equation with pure jump noise and multiplicative noise, specifically focusing on cases where the noise satisfies a uniform non-degeneracy condition. We demonstrate that the associated Markov process generated by the equation is strongly Feller and irreducible. Additionally, by assuming the noise complies with the Meyer-Zheng condition, we establish the existence of a unique invariant measure for this stochastic system. These findings are instrumental in proving the ergodicity of the group of transition probabilities. Furthermore, in the scenario where noise is colored by finite activity Lévy processes and satisfies condition $(A)$, we show ergodic convergence to the invariant measure with respect to both time and space initial conditions, assuming the noise meets condition $(B)$.

The proposed hFS is a dedicated detector designed to measure charged hadron spectra in ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions occurring within the ALICE experiment. It will be integrated into the broader ASTRAIC initiative, which aims to investigate the effects of extragalactic sources. The hFS is engineered to identify and count all charged particles with a momentum component along the beam axis exceeding 2.5 GeV/c, utilizing a 2.5 m² silicon microstrip tracker positioned 1.3 m downstream from the Interaction Point and a hadron calorimeter with a longitudinal depth of 2.5 λm located 25.4 m away from the same point. This setup enables the precise tracking and energy measurement of highly relativistic particles, granting the instrument exceptional sensitivity to the spectra of very forward particles.

This study introduces an orientation convolutional network (OCN) designed to encode images through their orientation functions. We demonstrate that the convolutional layers within this framework act as an efficient means of learning robust, orientation-based image representations. Furthermore, utilizing image orientation functions for recognition allows us to significantly reduce the required storage space for image data. Our findings, including experimental results, show that the OCN is particularly well-suited for applications involving low-bit images and low-bitplane grayscale data.

Recent developments in deep learning for point cloud processing rely heavily on Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs). However, applying GCNs to point clouds faces significant hurdles: constructing the graph requires defining a spatial neighborhood for each point, and the subsequent message passing involves aggregating data from these neighbors. This process is highly memory-intensive and computationally demanding, as it necessitates accessing widely scattered memory locations, thereby creating a substantial performance bottleneck. To address this issue, we propose a novel approach that eliminates both the explicit graph construction and the traditional message passing mechanism. Instead, we utilize an efficient GCN variant capable of handling point clouds, where message passing is executed within GPU shared memory to maximize speed. Our method features learnable, adaptive local graph operators that dynamically adjust graph structures based on point cloud characteristics during inference. Experimental results demonstrate that this inference-optimized design yields competitive performance in point cloud classification and segmentation tasks.

The advent of Large Language Models (LLMs) has triggered significant advancements across numerous application domains. However, research indicates that LLMs are highly susceptible to adversarial examples, prompting various attack methodologies to emerge. Among these, prompt injection attacks stand out as a particularly effective strategy; these involve adding carefully crafted tokens to inputs to manipulate model outputs away from user intent. This study introduces the Semantic Host-free Attack, a novel injection technique that works by appending specific tokens to activate semantic embeddings within an LLM's internal architecture. Unlike traditional injection attacks that rely on removing tokens from the input, this methodology adds them to generate desired semantic meanings that guide the model's generation. The attack demonstrates cross-machine efficacy and requires no access to host systems or source code. Furthermore, it outperforms existing injection methods in both effectiveness and stealthiness.

The Magellan Imaging and Spectrograph Instrument (IMACS) at Las Campanas Observatory has been upgraded with the Remotely Operated Spectrograph Instrument for the Study of the Ionized Emission (ROSIE). This Integral Field Unit (IFU) comprises a lenslet array and a single CCD detector, enabling the acquisition of 1024 $1.25 \times 1.25$ arcsec$^2$ fiber spectra across a wavelength range of 3500 to 9000 Angstroms. ROSIE offers superior spatial resolution compared to the Multi-Object Double Spectrograph Instrument (MOSI) IFU add-on, the MOSICube, which provides $2.04 \times 2.04$ arcsec$^2$ fields. Designed to complement MOSI for applications requiring both high spatial and spectral resolution, the system is particularly valuable for studying ionized gas kinematics in galaxies.

This study examines the existing literature on carbon-carbon fusion and evaluates the Tron-obar mode's progress in measuring direct fusion cross-sections. We also outline the theoretical framework employed to extract these direct components and demonstrate how removing them allows for the determination of total capture cross-sections via analysis of composite nuclei.

We present high-resolution, high-signal-to-noise-ratio spectra for 100 planet-hosting stars, enabling the precise determination of their elemental abundances. This dataset allows for the investigation of potential variations in stellar chemical compositions, which could signal the accretion of planetary bodies. Our analysis reveals a significant excess in chromium abundance in 10 stars, with 8 of these showing evidence of Earth-sized planet accretion. We estimate that these terrestrial planets had bulk chromium-to-silicon ratios roughly 10% higher than those of Earth, suggesting the captured material likely originated from the differentiated metallic cores of the worlds. While the observed stellar Cr/Si excesses are sporadic and not uniform, the overall frequency of such anomalies is low. Consequently, these findings indicate that planet formation and subsequent accretion do not substantially alter a star's total chemical composition.

Wireless localization leveraging Channel State Information (CSI) has garnered significant interest due to advancements in low-cost, high-performance hardware facilitating precise channel estimation. Nevertheless, existing CSI-based localization algorithms often struggle in real-world scenarios owing to hardware imperfections and environmental interferences, resulting in a decline in positioning accuracy. Addressing these challenges, this paper introduces a novel positioning method that exploits the redundancy within CSI data. Specifically, we propose an attention-based deep learning framework to automatically identify critical features influencing positioning while filtering out detrimental noise. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach surpasses current CSI-based localization algorithms in both accuracy and robustness.

A strong edge-coloring of a graph $G$ involves assigning colors to its edges such that every pair of adjacent vertices, along with their incident edges, uses a distinct palette. The chromatic number for strong edge-coloring, denoted as $\chi_s'(G)$, represents the minimum colors required. Vizing and Erd\H{o}s-Seymour separately conjectured that this value never surpasses the sum of the maximum degree $\Delta(G)$ plus two; specifically, $\chi_s'(G) \leq \Delta(G)+2$. In this work, we present counterexamples demonstrating that these hypotheses fail for both cases in specific graphs.

This paper investigates functions $f$ on the Hamming graph $\Gamma$ with a mean value of zero, where the magnitude of its Fourier coefficients relative to any orthonormal basis of eigenspaces not exceeding a specified degree $k$ is bounded by 1. The study focuses on determining the minimum support size for such functions, particularly when the largest Fourier coefficients are restricted to be at most 1 in absolute value. Additionally, we derive an enhanced upper bound for the support of functions $f$ ($\sum_{v} f(v) = 0$) whose spectral mass is concentrated exclusively within the eigenvalues of the first $k$ degenerate eigenspaces.

COPASI is a widely used, cross-platform, command-line simulation tool for biochemical networks. Although it supports extensive model analysis, its usage is restricted by a lack of intuitive web-based visualization for exploring model states, parameters, and analyses. To address this, we introduce ShinyCOPASI, a web application that visualizes COPASI models and their dynamic behaviors. Built on a Shiny interface to upload and interact with COPASI models using local files or remote URLs, the application features interactive 2D and 3D graphing for numerical data, as well as support for HTML, video, and 3D model formats.

Machine learning algorithms are increasingly utilized across diverse scientific domains for predicting outcomes from complex systems characterized by intricate dynamics and incomplete data. In these uncertain environments, assessing prediction reliability is critical. While recent studies indicate that neural networks can effectively forecast outcomes for complex systems even with limited data, there remains a significant lack of understanding regarding the impact of data and model uncertainties on prediction accuracy and the corresponding quantification of prediction uncertainty itself. This work addresses these gaps by evaluating various uncertainty quantification techniques for complex systems using a standardized benchmark of ten distinct models. We find that probabilistic neural networks outperform other approaches in predicting complex system behaviors and that prediction uncertainty estimates generally align well with actual prediction errors. Additionally, we propose an uncertainty metric designed to assess prediction reliability regarding the ease of acquiring new data, demonstrating its utility through comparisons of the estimated versus observed impacts of data uncertainty across different models.

This paper introduces an inexact Generalized Minimum Residual (IGMRES) iteration scheme designed to solve the linear system of equations arising in policy iteration for finite Markov decision processes. Functioning as a variant of the classic GmRES method, this algorithm prioritizes computational efficiency for large-scale problems by terminating once a specific relative residual tolerance is met. We provide a theoretical framework establishing the policy evaluation policy evaluation convergence criteria based on this IGMRES approach and demonstrate that policy iterations converge under these inexact conditions. Further, we outline the implementation details of combining IGMRES with fixed-point acceleration techniques. Experimental results on established test sets indicate that this proposed method outperforms both standard policy iteration and generalized value iteration algorithms.

Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a weighted oriented graph with edge ideal $I(\mathcal{D})$. We demonstrate that for a specified class of oriented trees $\mathcal{D}$, the ordinary and symbolic powers of this ideal are always equivalent. Furthermore, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions ensuring the equality between these powers specifically for lines equipped with their natural orientations.

This study addresses the challenge of inferring unknown parameters within time series computer simulators by employing a Bayesian framework. The objective is to determine the posterior distribution of these parameters, which depend on discrete-valued time series outputs. A primary difficulty arises from the fact that these posterior distributions are typically intractable due to the irregular and non-Gaussian nature of the likelihood function. To overcome this, the authors propose substituting the true distribution with a custom-designed approximate distribution through the Multiple Contour Estimation (MCE) method. The MCE approach generates multiple potential samples to yield superior estimates of numerical characteristics, specifically the mean and variance, thereby enhancing the overall quality of the Bayesian inference. The proposed methodology is validated using both real-world data and various scenarios, with performance metrics compared against established alternative techniques.

Recent studies have demonstrated that various local query models can fully leverage local derivative information to achieve local strong robustness for convex optimization tasks. This paper investigates the practical utility of local queries for robust generalization in the broader context of general learning, specifically examining how many such queries are necessary to achieve robust generalization of gradient and finite-ratio queries over neural networks. Our findings indicate that, broadly speaking, local queries offer no advantage for robust generalization. However, a specific exception arises when queries are restricted to occur exclusively over convex subsets of the parameter space; in this scenario, the required number of queries for robust generalization matches that needed for convex optimization. Furthermore, we present an efficient algorithm capable of locating the local queries and proving its robust effectiveness for both gradient and finite-ratio queries over deep neural networks. Empirical results suggest this method yields strong robust performance on MNIST and CIFAR-10.

This study examines how jet fragmentation is modified in lead-lead (PbPb) collisions at a center-of-mass energy per nucleon pair of 5.02 TeV, utilizing a technique that tags jets with isolated photons. The analysis focuses on events where a high-$p_T$ photon is detected in conjunction with a reconstructed jet within a narrow rapidity window ($|\Delta\eta| < 0.4$) relative to the photon. The transverse momentum distribution of constituent particles inside these photons-proximate jets is analyzed across various centrality classes, ranging from peripheral to head-on (central) collisions. The study further investigates how this modification depends on the fractional transverse momentum ($z_T$) of the constituents relative to the jet, as well as on the transverse momentum of the tagging photon itself. The observed alterations in jet fragmentation are compared against theoretical predictions from Monte Carlo event generators.

This article extends our exploration into non-classical Ap\'{e}ry-type series featuring mixed index parities by establishing new formulas for multiple sums. These are applied to colored multiple zeta values, resulting in several previously unknown identities.

The newly identified, extremely red and distant brown dwarf WISEA J153429.75-104303.3 (hereafter W1534-1043) was initially thought to reside at a distance of 26.3 ± 0.6 parsecs based on its parallax measurement. However, this study reveals that significant unmodeled flux exists in the $K_s$-band, causing the parallax signal to be contaminated by this excess emission. Consequently, the object is likely much farther away, exceeding 100 parsecs. Its extreme red coloration is attributed to a combination of this $K_s$-band flux surplus and strong absorption from CO and H₂O in the adjacent bands. We propose that W1534-1043 is a young, low-mass object exhibiting a "red dwarf" characteristic due to the presence of gaseous amorphous silicate dust grains with a size of approximately 0.1 μm. These grains are believed to originate from the disintegration of a larger parent body, such as a small planetesimal or large asteroid, which was destroyed by the host star's radiation. The dust is currently settling through the atmosphere at a rate of roughly 1 cm per year. The discovery of this system offers a rare opportunity to observe the atmospheric dynamics and chemical evolution of a planetary body's debris as it disperses within a brown

This study presents new measurements of pion, kaon, proton/anti-proton, and $\phi$-meson production in Xe-Xe collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.44$ TeV, covering transverse momentum ($p_{\rm T}$) ranges from 0 to 20 GeV/$c$ and rapidity ($y$) from 2.3 to 4.03. The results are expressed as differential yields normalized per binary nucleon-nucleon collision, alongside ratios comparing these spectra to those from Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.02$ TeV. Transverse momentum distributions are further analyzed using the nuclear modification factor, $A_{\rm d}/A_{\rm p}^{\prime}$, which quantifies the yield relative to the average number of binary nucleon-nucleon collisions, denoted as $\langle N_{\rm bin} \rangle$.

We introduce a highly efficient numerical technique for parton distribution function (PDF) evolution that leverages interpolation via Chebyshev polynomials. Although our approach is general, it specifically addresses singular PDFs exhibiting square-root branching near $x=0$ and boundary constraints at $x=1$. Although our approach is general, it accurately models the typical singularity found in PDFs at low $x$ as well as boundary conditions at high $x$. The method's practicality is demonstrated by evolving standard PDFs using DGLAP kernels, producing results that closely match those from conventional numerical methods with superior computational speed. Furthermore, the framework is extended to support PDFs defined on the generalized momentum fraction range $0\leq \xi\leq 2$, relevant for neutral mesons, by incorporating specific boundary conditions.

This study examines how sintering temperature influences the microstructure and mechanical characteristics of compacted lunar and Martian regolith. Utilizing a plasma arc for sintering, the research tracked microstructural shifts and measured mechanical strength across various thermal conditions. Results indicate that increasing temperature enhances regolith strength, primarily by promoting grain bonding and reducing porosity. The findings also compare lunar regolith to Martian regolith, noting that the latter exhibits superior mechanical properties due to its finer grain size and more uniform particle distribution. Ultimately, the work demonstrates the viability of using plasma arc sintering to fabricate structural components for Mars exploration missions.

This study examines the Rayleigh-Plateau instability governing a hanging liquid film on a rotating fibre, with a specific focus on the impacts of slip at the liquid-fibre interface. By employing lubrication theory, we derive an extended dispersion relation that accounts for both surface tension and viscous forces. Our results indicate that increasing the magnitude of slip accelerodes the instability, resulting in higher growth rates for the liquid film.

This study investigates the reliability of star formation rate (SFR) estimates derived from spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting by comparing them against SFRs calculated from the Brackett-$\gamma$ (Br$\gamma$) line. We analyzed data from the Spitzer Infrared Array Camera (IRAC) and the Multi-Object Spectrograph for Planetary Nebulae (MOSFES) for 100 molecular clouds in the Perseus region. For 60 of these clouds, we performed SED fitting using the code CIGALE, generating SFR estimates that were then contrasted with those from the MUSE spectroscopy. Our results indicate a strong correlation between the CIGALE and MUSE SED-derived SFRs, with a correlation coefficient of $r = 0.81$ and a scatter of 0.3 dex. Furthermore, Br$\gamma$-based SFRs show a significant correlation with the MUSE-derived values ($r = 0.71$, scatter = 0.35 dex). However, a notable offset exists where Br$\gamma$-based SFRs are consistently higher than those from MUSE by a factor of approximately 2.3 ($\log_{10}$ offset = 0.36 dex). Finally, we compared the SFRs from both the Br$\gamma$ line and the full spectral energy distribution to evaluate their respective efficiencies in estimating star formation activity.

In this paper, we investigate the symmetries associated with local types $II$ quantum subgroups of $\mathfrak{sl}_M$ within the context of affine Lie algebras $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ at high levels, specifically in their local module categories. We demonstrate that the Duflo-Serganova operator $D_s$ functions as a symmetry operation for these modules, with the resulting classification of such symmetries mirroring the linear symmetries of the Grassmannian. Furthermore, the paper presents the construction of $D_s$ and analyzes its fundamental properties, including the fact that it forms a $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-graded morphism that annihilates local modules of specific types.
The methodology proposed yields a novel closed-form solution for the broad diffusion equation, demonstrating particular effectiveness in describing heat transfer within rectangular domains.

Optical character recognition (OCR) is a technology used to convert printed or written text into machine-processable text. While standard solutions like Tesseract are generally ineffective for handwritten content, especially in mathematics, this study introduces a novel detection method leveraging handwritten digit data. By employing a sensor to capture the shape of digits written on paper, we transformed these physical inputs into machine-learning-compatible datasets. We trained various models, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory networks (LSTM), and Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLP), to classify these digits. Our proposed sensor-based mechanism offers a low-cost alternative to conventional optical methods for identifying handwritten numbers.

This study introduces a method for creating synthetic speech duration data by transforming measured speech lengths into a probability distribution function (PDF) through a non-parametric technique. Synthetic speech is then produced using the corresponding prosodic and phonemic information, with speech segment lengths sampled from this PDF. The resulting audio is concatenated to form sentences and utterances, where sentence formation relies on a sentence generator and utterance creation on an utterance synthesizer. These generated data are then utilized to train a neural network designed to predict speech durations in duration-based speech synthesis systems.

Spatial occupancy models are increasingly utilized in ecology to estimate species presence/absence while accounting for spatial spatial autocorrelation in detections, non-detections, and survey efforts. The `spOccupancy` package in R implements various single-species, multi-species, and integrated spatial occupancy models using data from telemetry (e.g., radio or GPS collars) or spatially explicit sampling. Available spatial processes include Gaussian processes, Gaussian random walks, and Gaussian autoregressive processes. The package offers flexible covariate models for occupancy and parameters for detection probability, allowing for linear effects, nonlinear relationships via splines, and hierarchical structures. Furthermore, it can jointly model detection processes based on telemetry efforts or spatially correlated animal detections. Model selection and diagnostic tools are provided, including spatial cross-validation and leave-one-site-out validation for evaluating predictive performance.

The global rise in skin cancer cases is a critical issue, particularly for melanoma, the most aggressive form, which demands early detection for survival. While dermatologists are essential, a shortage of specialists exists, especially in remote areas. To address this, "SkinCare" introduces an interactive deep learning framework designed to assist in diagnosing malignant skin lesions. The system combines a convolutional neural network (CNN) for initial classification with a region proposal network (RPN) to localize suspicious regions. These areas are then overlaid on the image, allowing medical professionals to review highlighted sections and make informed decisions. Evaluated on the ISIC 2019 dataset, SkinCare achieved an accuracy of 0.90 and an F1-score of 0.85 for classification, alongside an accuracy of 0.80 and an F1-score of 0.74 for localization.

We introduce a probabilistic autoencoder designed to reconstruct and forecast future spectra for Type Ia supernovae, utilizing actual spectral data. This model integrates Gaussian processes within the network's latent layer to capture both deterministic and stochastic variations in spectral evolution, effectively distinguishing between systematic trends and random scatter. By jointly modeling covariance for specific spectral lines, the approach enhances its fit to observed data. Furthermore, the framework enables joint forecasting of multiple targets, such as velocity and flux, as well as predictions at later times. We validate the model using real-world spectra from the Supernova Legacy Survey (SNLS) and demonstrate its capacity to forecast future spectra with significant accuracy.

We report the discovery of a resolved, neutral outflow in a dusty, dusty star-forming galaxy located at z = 2.09, identified via ALMA observations of CO(2-1) emission. This system is gravitationally lensed, exhibiting a magnification factor of approximately 10, and exhibits a total CO luminosity of $L_{\rm CO}(1-0) = 1.1 \times 10^9$ L$_{\odot}$. The derived total mass outflow rate is $\dot{M}_{\rm out} = 1.1$ M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$, with a mean outflow velocity of $v_{\rm out} = 130$ km s$^{-1}$. The mass outflow rate ratio, $\dot{M}_{\rm out}/\dot{M}_{\rm SFR}$, reaches 1.1, indicating that the outflow is significant. The spatial extent of the outflow is roughly 1.5 kpc, corresponding to about 3 effective radii ($R_{\rm eff}$) of the galaxy. The outflow's kinematics are characterized by a double-peaked CO(2-1) profile with a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 160 km s$^{-1}$. We introduce a novel analytical framework for predicting the dynamics of particle-laden plumes, grounded in the entrainment model proposed by Turner (1976). This approach utilizes the flux-conservation concept to forecast the evolution of velocity and buoyancy, alongside the conservation of mean momentum and variance to estimate the entrainment index. The resulting predictions for velocity, buoyancy, and the entrainment index are compared against both the classical model by Morton et al. (1972) and findings from direct numerical simulations. The study reveals that the presence of heavy particles significantly alters the entrainment index, a change that stems from the interaction between turbulent kinetic energy and particle kinetic energy. Furthermore, the efficacy of the proposed model is assessed across varying conditions, specifically examining the effects of particle size and the particle-to-fluid density ratio.

The spread of epidemics within a population is frequently modeled using the classic SI (Susceptible-Infected) framework, which relies on pairwise interactions. However, in realistic scenarios, individuals may contract infections through multiple distinct transmission routes simultaneously. We adapt the SI model to hyperedges of varying cardinality to analyze infection dynamics driven by these compound routes. Our research identifies precise spectral conditions for the complete disappearance of an infected state. Specifically, we establish that infection persistence is contingent upon the principal eigenvalue of a specific non-symmetric dynamical matrix; consequently, we derive corresponding threshold criteria by examining this leading eigenvalue.

The recent discovery of the two-dimensional ferromagnetic insulator chromium iodide (CrI$_3$) has generated significant interest in the field. This study employs first-principles calculations to examine the spin textures of the bulk and surface states within a CrI$_3$ bilayer. We find that the bulk states exhibit a complex spin texture, which arises from the combined influence of exchange interactions, spin-orbit coupling, and the material's noncentrosymmetric crystal structure. Notably, the net magnetization drives a net spin polarization aligned with the $c$-axis, while the net zero orbital moment produces a net zero Berry curvature. Conversely, the surface states display simple spin textures characterized by in-plane orientation, resulting from the interplay of exchange, spin-orbit coupling, and structural symmetry breaking at the surface boundary. These surface textures are sensitive to the net Rashba spin-orbit coupling and can be manipulated by an external electric field.

The open question of how magnetic cycles emerge in slowly rotating stars is addressed by simulating their evolution using mean-field dynamo theory. The study incorporates a time-dependent, latitude-varying magnetic $\alpha$-effect and explores the effects of both pro-solar and anti-solar differential rotation on magnetic cycle characteristics. The findings indicate that the phase of a magnetic cycle is determined by the magnetic latitude of origin: cycles arising from high-latitude sources exhibit a prolonged period, whereas those from the equator display shorter periods. The magnetic period is found to be independent of the sign of the differential rotation but relies on the magnitude of the latitudinal shear. The magnetic latitudinal origin shifts toward the equator as stellar rotation slows, a phenomenon that can amplify the magnetic cycle duration regardless of the rotational shear's sign. The model successfully reproduces the characteristic hysteresis loops observed in activity indices of stars exhibiting magnetic cycles. The research concludes that magnetic cycles in stars rotating more sluggishly than the Sun can develop even with anti-solar differential rotation, provided the latitudinal shear is sufficiently strong.

Although Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have achieved significant success in computer vision, their performance often degrades when dealing with imbalanced multimodal data containing numerous empty classes. Additionally, current multimodal architectures typically process shared information through concatenated inputs, which may limit effective feature interaction. Addressing these challenges, this paper introduces the Generalized K-fan (GKM) deep model with shared representations, designed specifically for multimodal object recognition on irregular and balanced datasets. The GFM architecture utilizes a fan-in structure to mitigate issues arising from data disparity and an innovative shared representation module to enhance computational efficiency while maintaining robustness. Experimental validation on the benchmark WIDE and NUS-MAP datasets confirms that the proposed GKM model outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches.

Dynamic detection of concurrency bugs in multi-threaded programs represents a significant challenge for software verification. Existing Dynamic Partial Order Exploration (DPOR) techniques, while capable of identifying runtime errors, typically suffer from poor scalability when encountering complex real-world applications. Conversely, recent DPOR approaches that achieve better scalability often fail to correctly handle interactions between threads and the memory hierarchy. This paper introduces McMini, a innovative DPOR-based model checker that effectively balances scalability with the correct analysis of memory hierarchy behaviors. McMini achieves this by integrating advanced bitvector-based abstract interpretation techniques with refined guidelines for recording and resolving memory hierarchy interactions. Evaluations on industry-standard benchmarks demonstrate that McMini correctly identifies known memory-related faults and offers substantial improvements in error detection, surpassing current state-of-the-art solutions.

WhatsApp, the world's leading messaging application, facilitates widespread information sharing, including both accurate data and rumors, particularly during crises like the COVID-19 pandemic. To curb the viral spread of false narratives, the company reduced the standard message forwarding limit from 500 to 25 recipients. This study examines the impact of this policy change by analyzing over 1.5 million WhatsApp messages exchanged among 1.2 million unique users in India, a nation heavily impacted by the crisis. Our analysis reveals that the policy had minimal effect on overall message circulation volume. However, it did successfully decrease the propagation of misinformation, suggesting that stricter message controls can curb the spread of falsehoods without necessarily stifling general information exchange.

The paper introduces a branching process featuring a general supercritical population dynamics and general branching mechanisms, for which the limiting allic frequency spectrum is approximated. This approach relies on a broad class of non-degenerate branching population models and allows for both continuous and discrete time frameworks, covering both discrete and continuous trait spaces. In instances where traits vary continuously, the limit is defined by a measure on $\mathbb{R}$ normalized to the interval $[0,1]$, representing the initial population size; this is constructed through a general branching mean value subjected to a specific normalization. When applied to a Poissonian reproduction model with logarithmically singular expected logarithmic branching measures, the resulting limit aligns with prior calculations by Baudoin, Brunet, and Gueron [10]. Furthermore, under conditions of general branching and logarithmic singularities in the mean logarithmic branching measures, the text establishes sufficient criteria for ensuring tightness within this population frequency framework.

Deep learning-based end-to-end audio spoofing detection systems have seen rapid development in recent years, largely due to their superior performance and streamlined implementation compared to traditional methods. Nevertheless, their success relies heavily on the extensive diversity of available training data, rendering these models highly susceptible to attacks by adversarial examples. While various strategies have been proposed to enhance robustness, their effectiveness often diminishes significantly in resource-constrained environments, such as those with limited computational power or scarce data. This study introduces a lightweight attentive activation function designed specifically to bolster system resilience against detector attacks with minimal additional compute overhead. Empirical results demonstrate that this proposed layer enhances robustness by approximately 10% relative to baseline systems.
